entities.summary: Sixtus of Tannberg was a pivotal figure in the medieval European clergy, serving as both Bishop of Gurk from 1470 to 1474 and Prince-Bishop of Freising from 1474 to 1495. During his tenure, he played a significant role in the governance of the region, implementing various reforms and expanding the influence of the Catholic Church. His leadership contributed to the stability and prosperity of the region, shaping the course of local history for centuries to come. Notably, Sixtus of Tannberg was a key figure in the Protestant Reformation, as he was a prominent supporter of Martin Luther's ideas, which would eventually lead to the establishment of the Lutheran Church in Germany. His legacy as a reformer and leader of the clergy has endured, with historians continuing to study his impact on the development of the Protestant movement.
